statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-32288 (GO-2026-4869): in the Go standard library's archive/tar package, tar.Reader can allocate an unbounded amount of memory reading a crafted archive with a very large number of sparse regions in the old GNU sparse map format. It is fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4869, https://go.dev/issue/78301, https://go.dev/cl/763766, the release-branch.go1.26 backport https://github.com/golang/go/commit/a34b5e4d55e39efc9af0d803969e9399a553acf3 (in go1.26.2, not go1.26.1), https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU . We read every published alertmanager-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to 0.35.0-r2, x86_64 and aarch64, each download checked against the repository index checksum. Each package holds two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the Go Cryptographic Module (GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c) and linked with -s -w, so we read their function tables from the Go line table, which works on these stripped binaries, and found runtime.main in every one. The Go toolchain recorded in the build information, the same for both programs and both architectures, is: 0.31.1-r0 with Go 1.25.7; 0.31.1-r1 to 0.31.1-r4 with Go 1.26.1; 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r0 with Go 1.26.2; 0.32.1-r1 to 0.32.1-r2 with Go 1.26.3; 0.32.1-r3 to 0.33.1-r0 with Go 1.26.4; 0.33.1-r1 to 0.33.1-r3 with Go 1.26.5; 0.33.1-r5 to 0.34.0-r0 with Go 1.26.6; 0.34.0-r1 with Go 1.26.7; 0.34.0-r2 to 0.34.1-r1 with Go 1.26.8; 0.34.1-r2 to 0.34.1-r3 with Go 1.26.9; 0.34.1-r4 to 0.35.0-r0 with Go 1.26.10; 0.35.0-r1 to 0.35.0-r2 with Go 1.26.11. The vulnerable code is in the archive/tar package (Reader.Next, Reader.readOldGNUSparseMap and readGNUSparseMap1x0). In no build does either program's function table contain any archive/tar function, and a search of the bytes of every binary, which also finds the names of inlined functions, finds no archive/tar. name (the form in which Go records that package's functions and methods). As a positive control, the same two checks on a program we built with Go 1.26.1 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 that reads a tar archive find Reader.Next, Reader.readOldGNUSparseMap and readGNUSparseMap1x0 in its function table and archive/tar. names in its bytes. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.

It is fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4869, https://go.dev/issue/78301, https://go.dev/cl/763766 and https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU give the details, and the release-branch.go1.26 commit https://github.com/golang/go/commit/a34b5e4d55e39efc9af0d803969e9399a553acf3 names this CVE and is in go1.26.2 but not go1.26.1. We downloaded every published package built from the build-fips source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository, which requires authentication: build-fips (91 builds, 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0) and build-fips-dev (91 builds, 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0), on x86_64 and aarch64, except 2.6.4-r0, published for aarch64 only; each package was checked against its index checksum. 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves, the only one that matches its listed checksum, was the one read. Every build-fips-dev package holds only /usr/bin/build. In the build-fips packages the programs are: /usr/bin/build in 2.6.4-r0 to 2.26.2-r0; /opt/docker/dhi/yq and /usr/bin/build in 2.26.2-r1 to 2.27.1-r0; /opt/docker/dhi/uv, /opt/docker/dhi/yq and /usr/bin/build in 2.27.1-r1 to 2.28.0-r0; /opt/docker/dhi/uv, /opt/docker/dhi/yq, /usr/bin/build and /usr/bin/dhi-source in 2.28.0-r1 to 2.30.0-r0. /opt/docker/dhi/uv is not a Go program: it has no Go build information or Go function table. Every other program is a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, and all Go programs in one build use the same Go release. The Go release in each build, the same in every package and on both architectures, is: 2.6.4-r0 to 2.6.6-r1 with Go 1.25.7; 2.7.0-r1 to 2.8.3-r0 with Go 1.25.8; 2.8.3-r1 to 2.9.2-r0 with Go 1.26.1; 2.10.0-r0 to 2.15.0-r0 with Go 1.26.2; 2.15.0-r1 to 2.17.3-r0 with Go 1.26.3; 2.17.3-r1 to 2.20.0-r2 with Go 1.26.4; 2.20.0-r3 to 2.20.0-r5 with Go 1.26.5; 2.20.0-r6 with Go 1.26.6; 2.20.0-r7 to 2.20.0-r10 with Go 1.26.7; 2.20.0-r11 to 2.26.0-r0 with Go 1.26.8; 2.26.0-r1 to 2.26.1-r0 with Go 1.26.9; 2.26.1-r1 to 2.28.0-r2 with Go 1.26.10; 2.28.0-r3 to 2.30.0-r0 with Go 1.26.11. The function table of /usr/bin/build lists Reader.Next, Reader.readOldGNUSparseMap and readGNUSparseMap1x0 in archive/tar in every build that ships it (runtime.main found in each as a control); /opt/docker/dhi/yq and /usr/bin/dhi-source do not, so the vulnerable code is linked and the Go release decides. In the builds we also searched for the bare text, external-dns 0.20.0-r0, 0.21.0-r0 and 0.24.0-r5 for x86_64 and 0.21.0-r1 for aarch64, archive/tar occurs once, as a package name in the Go standard library's table of GODEBUG settings, which a program we built with Go 1.26.1 that does not import archive/tar contains as well; it is data, not archive/tar code. Both checks find runtime.main in every binary. As a positive control, the same two checks on a program we built with Go 1.26.1 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 that reads a tar archive find archive/tar.(*Reader).Next, (*Reader).readOldGNUSparseMap and readGNUSparseMap1x0. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this owner.

The range ends at 1.26.2-r3, the first build that carries the fix.
